Decision card · ord-001
Outcome: Not yet known (facts needed) · not safe to act
Why:
- The Medicare billing/coding guidance (A58982 for LCD L39237) requires specific coverage criteria for ESAs in CKD not on dialysis (diagnosis D63.1 plus an appropriate CKD code such as N18.32, and serum creatinine and/or GFR) — those diagnoses and eGFR are present for this patient (D63.1, N18.32, eGFR 38) (A58982, pp. 9–11).
- The same guidance requires that iron stores be evaluated prior to ESA initiation (transferrin saturation ≥20% and ferritin ≥100 ng/mL) and documented before starting therapy; those iron study results are not present in the patient facts provided (A58982, pp. 10–11).
Next step: Obtain and document pre-initiation iron studies (TSAT and ferritin) and ensure the serum creatinine/GFR documentation is included with the claim; once iron stores meet the required thresholds and documentation is assembled, re-evaluate for coverage/authorization.
Source: Billing and Coding Article A58982, Erythropoiesis Stimulating Agents (for L39237) — Required documentation and CKD (non-dialysis) coverage criteria, pages 9–11; code group listing including J0885, page 17.

Why: Patient and order meet many Medicare coverage elements for J0885 (CKD not on dialysis; D63.1 and N18.32 present; pre-initiation Hgb 9.4 < 10) — but documentation requirements for ESA initiation include iron studies (TSAT >= 20% and ferritin >= 100 ng/mL) and evaluation/treatment of other causes of anemia, which are not present in the journey facts.

Decision card · ord-002
Outcome: Other gate (coverage criteria not met) · not safe to act
Why: The Medicare billing/coding guidance for ESAs in CKD-not-on-dialysis requires specific CKD staging/GFR criteria; patients with CKD stage IIIa (eGFR ~45–59) do not meet the GFR requirements for coverage with the D63.1 + CKD diagnosis combinations. The patient’s eGFR is 52 (CKD stage IIIa), so the coverage GFR threshold is not met despite Hb <10 g/dL.
Next step: Do not administer under this coverage rule. Staff should consider alternative management (e.g., evaluate for transfusion or treat reversible causes of anemia), or confirm whether the patient has a different billed CKD diagnosis code meeting the coverage list (e.g., N18.32, N18.4, N18.5, I12.x/I13.x) or other documentation that would satisfy coverage; if provider believes coverage applies, submit supporting clinical documentation for medical review/exception.
Source: Billing and Coding Article A58982, “Erythropoiesis Stimulating Agents (for L39237)”, pages 10–11 (requirements for CKD not on dialysis; GFR threshold and note that patients with stage I, II and IIIa CKD do not meet GFR requirements).

Decision card · ord-002
Outcome: Other gate (coverage criteria not met) · not safe to act
Why: Patient has HCPCS J0885 (epoetin alfa) for CKD not on dialysis but does not meet the LCD required CKD staging/GFR codes — the billing guidance for non-dialysis CKD requires D63.1 plus CKD codes such as N18.32, N18.4, or N18.5 (stage 3b–5); the patient has N18.31 (CKD stage 3a), which is not an accepted code for coverage. (Patient’s eGFR 52 mL/min/1.73 m2 is above the GFR threshold cited.) 
Next step: Staff should contact the ordering provider to (a) confirm/obtain a CKD diagnosis code that matches the LCD coverage requirements (N18.32, N18.4, N18.5) or provide documentation supporting use despite stage 3a (e.g., documentation of GFR trend or other qualifying conditions), or (b) consider alternative treatment or coding. If additional clinical facts (e.g., recent confirmatory GFR/creatinine showing lower GFR or alternate qualifying diagnosis) are provided, re-evaluate for possible coverage or PA.
Source: Billing and Coding Article A58982 (supports LCD L39237) — Required documentation and CKD non-dialysis criteria, pages 10–11.

Decision card · ord-002
Outcome: Other gate (coverage criteria not met) · not safe to act
Why: The billing guidance for ESAs in CKD not on dialysis requires both (1) D63.1 and (2) a CKD diagnosis code indicating more advanced CKD (examples listed include N18.32, N18.4, N18.5) and/or a GFR threshold supporting ESA use; the patient has D63.1 but has N18.31 (CKD 3a) and eGFR 52 mL/min/1.73 m2 which does not meet the stated GFR threshold (<45 mL/min/1.73 m2) supporting ESA initiation.
Next step: Do not administer under current Medicare coverage; staff should either (a) obtain updated documentation/labs showing a lower eGFR or an eligible CKD diagnosis code (or documentation of dialysis status if applicable), or (b) consider alternative management (transfusion/other therapies) and/or discuss appeal/medical review if clinical justification exists.
Source: Billing and Coding Article A58982, “Erythropoiesis Stimulating Agents (for L39237)”, pages 10–11 — required documentation, GFR threshold guidance, and list of accepted CKD diagnosis codes for CKD not on dialysis (J0885).

Decision card · ord-002
Outcome: Other gate (coverage criteria not met) · not safe to act
Why: The Palmetto LCD L39237 limits non‑ESRD ESA coverage to CKD stages IIIb, IV and V (not stage 3a); patient has N18.31 / eGFR 52 which is CKD stage 3a (LCD L39237, pp.5-6).
Why: The billing article for L39237 requires specific CKD diagnosis codes (e.g., N18.32, N18.4, N18.5) to support J0885 for non‑dialysis CKD; N18.31 is not listed as an accepted code (A58982, p.10).
Next step: Do not authorize. Ask clinical staff to provide documentation of a covered indication — e.g., confirm a qualifying CKD stage (IIIb/IV/V) or submit an alternate covered diagnosis (chemotherapy-induced anemia, AZT-related anemia, low‑risk MDS, or peri‑surgical use) with supporting labs/notes — then re-review.
Source: LCD L39237 Erythropoiesis Stimulating Agents (Palmetto GBA), pp.5-6; Billing & Coding Article A58982 (for L39237), p.10.

Decision card · ord-003
Outcome: No PA · safe to act
Why: Original Medicare coverage for erythropoiesis-stimulating agents is governed by the Medicare LCD/article (L39237 / A58982) and identifies J0885 as the HCPCS code for non‑ESRD use; the policy describes clinical coverage criteria (including hemoglobin/hematocrit targets) rather than a prior authorization requirement (A58982 discusses billing/modifier and medical necessity review but does not impose a PA) (see sources).
Next step: Proceed with the order; ensure medical record documents diagnosis (CKD non‑dialysis N18.31 / D63.1), current hemoglobin (9.4 g/dL), intent of therapy, and report the appropriate ESA modifier (EC for non‑cancer, non‑chemotherapy use) on the claim per A58982.
Source: Article A58982 (Billing & Coding: Erythropoiesis Stimulating Agents), pages 5, 6, 17 — shows J0885 is for non‑ESRD use, hemoglobin/hematocrit targets, modifier requirements and that coverage is determined by medical necessity rather than a PA; also governed by LCD L39237 (see LCD L39237, page 4).

Decision card · ord-003
Outcome: Other gate (coverage criteria not met) · not safe to act
Why: The Medicare billing/coding guidance for ESAs (A58982 / L39237) requires documentation of CKD-related anemia (D63.1) AND supports ESA use for CKD-not-on-dialysis patients typically when GFR is below ~45 mL/min/1.73 m2; the patient’s eGFR is 52, which does not meet that reasonable-threshold criterion.
Next step: Staff should either (a) supply additional documentation justifying ESA use despite eGFR>45 (e.g., transfusion dependence, symptomatic anemia with supporting literature, other compelling clinical evidence) or (b) withhold ESA administration / submit denial and pursue appeal with supporting records. Ensure the claim will include the EC modifier and required labs (serum creatinine/GFR, iron studies) per CMS guidance.
Source: Billing & Coding Article A58982 (Erythropoiesis Stimulating Agents), pages 6 and 10 — required ICD D63.1 for CKD not on dialysis, EC modifier requirement, and GFR <45 mL/min/1.73 m2 cited as a reasonable threshold to support ESA administration.

Decision card · ord-004
Outcome: PA required · not safe to act
Why: Injectafer (HCPCS J1439) is listed as a non-preferred intravenous iron product under the UnitedHealthcare MA Part B Step Therapy policy; non-preferred IV iron (Injectafer) may be covered only when step-therapy criteria are met (trial of at least 3 weeks of at least two preferred IV iron therapies, or documented contraindication/intolerance to at least two preferred therapies, or continuation of prior therapy within 365 days). The chart/facts do not show those required prior trials or contraindications.
Next step: Staff should submit a prior authorization request with documentation showing either (a) trials of at least 3 weeks each of two preferred IV iron therapies (iron sucrose J1756, sodium ferric gluconate J2916, or ferumoxytol Q0138) with minimal response, OR (b) documented contraindication/intolerance to at least two preferred IV iron therapies, OR (c) evidence of continuation of prior therapy within the past 365 days.
Source: UnitedHealthcare Medicare Advantage Drug Policy IAP.001.30, “Intravenous Iron Replacement Therapy” (pages 8, 18).
